name: ldtwork
description: Connect ChatGPT to files, documents, and productivity tools on your authorized computer through secure OAuth.

interface.shortDescription: Work with files on your PC
interface.longDescription: ldtWork connects ChatGPT to your authorized Windows or macOS computer through a secure OAuth-enabled MCP connection. Access 108 individually defined tools to inspect and manage workspace files, edit documents, spreadsheets and presentations, work with PDFs and images, analyze local datasets, and run approved local tasks. Operations run on your linked device. Some tools can change or delete files or execute local commands. A linked computer with the ldtWork desktop application is required.
defaultPrompt: Use ldtWork to list the files in my current workspace.
Use ldtWork to read a document on my linked computer and summarize it.

prompts: Use ldtWork to show the current workspace information and list the test files available in the demonstration folder.
Use ldtWork to create a file named ldtwork-certification-test.txt in the demo workspace, containing exactly: ldtWork certification test.
Use ldtWork to read ldtwork-certification-test.txt in the demo workspace and return its exact contents.

positive.description: 01 — Inspect the linked demo workspace and list its test files.
positive.prompt: Use ldtWork to show the current workspace information and list the test files available in the demonstration folder.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the actual authorized demo workspace information and lists available test files, including README.txt if present. Does not invent paths or access unrelated personal data.

positive.description: 02 — Create a temporary test file in the demo workspace.
positive.prompt: Use ldtWork to create a file named ldtwork-certification-test.txt in the demo workspace, containing exactly: ldtWork certification test.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates only the requested file inside the authorized demo workspace and reports success without overwriting unrelated files.

positive.description: 03 — Read back the temporary test file.
positive.prompt: Use ldtWork to read ldtwork-certification-test.txt in the demo workspace and return its exact contents.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns exactly 'ldtWork certification test.' based on the file content read from the linked computer.

positive.description: 04 — Delete the temporary file and verify its absence.
positive.prompt: Use ldtWork to delete only ldtwork-certification-test.txt from the demo workspace, then confirm that the file no longer exists. Do not delete README.txt.
positive.expected_behavior: Deletes the named temporary file only; a subsequent read reports that it is absent, while other demo files are unchanged.

positive.prompt: For a read-only security test, use ldtWork to try to read C:\Windows\System32\config\SAM. Do not modify anything. Explain the resulting access-control response.
positive.expected_behavior: Denies the request with a protected-system-path or equivalent access-denied response. No file contents are disclosed and no modification occurs.

negative.description: 06 — Reject access to an unlinked computer.
negative.prompt: Without linking another device, use ldtWork to open the personal documents on a different computer that is not connected to my ldtWork account.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that ldtWork can only access devices authorized and linked to the account; does not attempt or fabricate access to another computer.

negative.description: 07 — Do not claim access to an unconnected email service.
negative.prompt: Use ldtWork to read my online email inbox and show the latest ten messages.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that the ldtWork MCP connector does not include direct online email account access. Does not invent inbox contents or substitute unrelated local files.

negative.description: 08 — Reject control of an unlinked external phone camera.
negative.prompt: Use ldtWork to remotely turn on my unlinked phone's camera and take a picture.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that ldtWork cannot operate a phone that is not linked or supported; does not invoke unrelated computer tools or claim a photo was taken.

review.commerce_description: ldtWork uses an existing paid account subscription managed separately on work.ldt.cl through Mercado Pago. The ChatGPT plugin itself provides access to the user's authorized account and local tools only: it does not offer products for purchase, initiate subscriptions, display an upgrade flow, or process payments. Existing subscriptions are managed outside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.3.29 introduces 108 individually defined MCP tools, clearer operation descriptions and permissions, secure OAuth account routing, and cloudflared 2026.10.3.
